metadata.title: [Model][SM70] DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 on 8x V100: EXL3 experts, graph attention, DSpark speculative decoding, 1M context (stacks on #1031)
metadata.body:
## DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 on 8× V100-SXM2-32GB: EXL3 experts, graph-captured attention, DSpark speculative decoding, 1M context

This stacks on #1031 (`feat/deepseek-v41-sm70`, the PP2×TP4 / PP3×TP4 bring-up; its 5 commits are included here unchanged) and takes the port from the 2.8–3.9 tok/s eager baseline to a usable server on a single 8-GPU V100 box. Everything below was measured on 8× V100-SXM2-32GB (NVLink, PP2×TP4, Xeon 64c / 372 GB).

### What is added

**EXL3 routed experts (`csrc/sm70_turbomind/ops/exl3_moe_sm70.cu`, `quantization/exl3.py`, `sm70/moe_exl3.py`).** Loads exllamav3 trellis checkpoints with per-expert bit widths (K = 2..5, codebook `mul1`), decodes the trellis inside the MoE GEMV (nothing dequantized to memory), expert-parallel inside the TP group (whole experts per rank, load-balanced by routing histogram). A grouped kernel decodes each expert once per ≤ 8 routed slots; `VLLM_DS41_MOE_EXL3_GROUP_MIN_TOKENS` (default 65) selects it from that many tokens. Test: `tests/kernels/quantization/test_exl3_moe.py`.

**Graph-captured decode attention (`sm70/sparse.py`, `sm70/sparse_kernels.py`, `attention.py`).** Per-layer CUDA graphs with device-side metadata builders (window rows, compressed-latent slots, state rows computed by kernels into static buffers; no host decisions), split-K fused decode attention over the packed FP4 compressed KV, graph-captured builders. Knobs `VLLM_DS41_ATTN_GRAPH`, `VLLM_DS41_BUILDER_GRAPHS`, `VLLM_DS41_ATTN_OUTER_GRAPH`.

**Hyper-connection kernels (`sm70/hc_kernels.py`, `common/hc.py`).** Fused bit-exact `hc_pre` / `hc_post`, fused Sinkhorn split, optional fused mixes.

**Engram host service (`common/engram_host.py`, `common/engram.py`).** Rows gathered on the host from the 189 GB tables (pinned, double-buffered), deferred zero-copy variant for async scheduling, exact FP8 row decode and gate kernels; hardened timeouts so a host I/O stall delays a step instead of killing the engine.

**DSpark speculative decoding (`sm70/dspark.py`, `v1/spec_decode/dspark.py`, `gpu_model_runner.py`).** The port's 3 MTP blocks as a DSpark drafter: PP + synchronous scheduling + spec decode bookkeeping (non-last stages receive every token they lack after accepted drafts), Engram step planner for multi-token steps, drafter attention captured from static per-layer context (each drafter layer's own KV group / block table), padded blocks clamped. Drafter graphs: plain `CUDAGraphWrapper` per batch size in their own pool, eager during the memory-profiling pass, and the drafter's all-reduces on NCCL: the custom all-reduce inside the drafter graph faulted with an illegal memory access at the second batch size (its IPC-registered buffers are looked up by pointer; the drafter graph at a new batch size all-reduces an unregistered buffer). Disabling the custom all-reduce only during the drafter call keeps the main model's fast path. `max_num_seqs` 2–4 verified exact (concurrent greedy 6/6, 9/9 identical to single-request).

**Batch-invariant dense GEMMs (`sm70/fixed_m.py`, `VLLM_DS41_BATCH_INVARIANT_GEMM`, default off).** cuBLAS selects the kernel by M; on V100 fp16 the rows of a 14-row GEMM differ from a 13-row call in the last ulp for about half the elements, and through 40 MoE layers at 2.8 bpw that became up to 2.5 nats between a prompt prefilled alone and the same prompt prefilled alongside other requests' decode rows (mean KL 0.12 on short prompts). Padding the row count to fixed buckets (≤16 → 16, else ×64, owning outputs, also under graph capture) at the port's GEMM call sites makes lone prefills bit-exact and takes mixed-step KL to 0.013, with no measurable speed cost. The same class as DeepInfer's `DEEPINFER_BATCH_INVARIANT`.

**Packed FP4 compressed KV, 1M context.** Native 1,048,576-token context fits (1.29–1.39M-token KV pool at `--max-num-batched-tokens 1024`).

### Measured (8× V100, PP2×TP4, EXL3 ~2.8 bpw experts)

| Configuration | Decode |
|---|---|
| Plain decode, 1 stream | 30.5 tok/s (from 2.8 eager at the #1031 base; 20.75 before graphs) |
| Plain decode, 4 streams | 63–74 tok/s aggregate |
| DSpark k=5, 1 stream: code / structured / prose / chat | 66–68 / 71 / 33–40 / 31 tok/s on completion-style prompts (see the DSpark note below for chat) |
| DSpark, 2 streams | 76–79 tok/s aggregate |
| Prefill | ~900 tok/s plain, ~560–600 with DSpark; 256K-token needle PASS |

Quality: KL 0.036 vs DeepSeek's own `inference/model.py` run in fp32 on CPU (3,134 positions, 8 domains), top-1 95.6 %; greedy outputs bit-identical between single and batched decode; step-wise decode vs one-pass prefill self-consistency KL ≤ 0.05 mean.

**DSpark in chat (known issue in this PR, fixed in a later build).** The drafter's hidden-state taps are captured in fp16. On the attention-sink tokens at the start of a chat they overflow to inf, which leaves NaN rows in the drafter's window, so for roughly the first 100 steps of a chat the drafts are all zeros (42 % of steps overall). Completion-style prompts have no BOS and never hit it, which is why the table above didn't show it. Scaling the taps down before the fp16 cast fixes it: NaN-draft steps go to 0 and first-draft acceptance on code goes from 0.49 to 0.90. That fix is not in this PR yet.

### Current build (not in this PR)

The engine has moved on since this PR was opened. The build we serve now also has decoder replay in prefill (layers 21–39 run only each request's last 3,072 rows, exact), fused WMMA sparse attention for prefill, a tiled EXL3 prefill MoE kernel, RAM-resident Engram tables, layer-sliced prefill between decode steps, fused indexer kernels, a graph-capturable fused decode indexer and the tap fix above. Each piece sits behind a `VLLM_DS41_*` knob and was gated against the fp32 oracle. That engine, as served, is published at [philbert440/deepseek-v4.1-v100](https://github.com/philbert440/deepseek-v4.1-v100) (tag `ds41-final-20261025`) for anyone who wants to run or review it. Measured on it:

| | |
|---|---|
| DSpark k=5, 1 stream, natural chat-template prompts: code / JSON / chat / prose | 64.9 / 65.9 / 35.0 / 34.5 tok/s |
| DSpark k=5, 2 streams aggregate: code / JSON / chat / prose | 95.5 / 103.3 / 57.3 / 52.3 tok/s |
| Decode at 8K / 128K context | 51.0 / 52.6 tok/s |
| Solo prefill at 8K / 32K / 128K | 2,985 / 3,231 / 3,194 tok/s |
| KL vs the fp32 oracle | 0.0358, top-1 95.79 % |

### Acknowledgement

This started from 0xSero's `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-EXL3-2.7bpw` pack: the first V4.1 pack that ran on 8×V100 and the baseline every change here was measured against. The published pack's base is HeNryous' 2.75 bpw with Mia-AiLab EAQ upgrades.

### Notes for reviewers

- Branch base is #1031's head (`a36df7c`); merges clean onto current `main` (no conflicts in `git merge-tree`), 497 commits behind.
- All new behaviour is behind `VLLM_DS41_*` knobs with the documented defaults; the generic vLLM paths are untouched except `gpu_model_runner.py` (drafter wrapper selection, PP spec-decode token accounting, profiling flag) and `v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` (PP spec-decode: send every token a non-last stage lacks).
- Diagnostic knobs (`DS41_DRAFT_NO_STATIC`, `DS41_DRAFT_NO_MOE`, `DS41_DRAFT_FORCE_STATIC`, `DS41_DEBUG_POS`) are default-off bisection aids; happy to drop them if preferred.
- Launchers, gates and the pack-building recipe live outside this repo; the matching expert pack is published on the Hub as `philbert440/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-EXL3-franken-v100`.
